big: When Meena buys a bond, she does not buy a piece of a company. She lends money. The borrower promises regular interest and the return of her money on a fixed date. That promise is the whole idea.

lines: So a bond is the opposite of a share?
Close. A share makes you an owner, with no promise. A bond makes you a lender, with a promise to pay interest and return the principal. The promise is only as good as the borrower.

note: At maturity, the investor also gets the ₹1,00,000 face value back.

title: Bond basics
stops: A bond is a loan to a government or company
A bondholder owns part of the company
The coupon is the regular interest on a bond
Face value is paid out every month
caps: The issuer promises interest and the return of the principal.
A bondholder is a lender, not an owner.
The coupon is stated as a percentage of face value.
Face value is repaid at maturity, once.

q: Rohan buys a bond with a face value of ₹1,00,000 and a 7% coupon. How much interest does he get each year?
why: ₹70,000 would be 70% of the face value, which is far too large.
₹700 would be only 0.7%, which is too small.
Seven percent of ₹1,00,000 is ₹7,000 each year.
₹1,07,000 adds the interest of one year to the face value.

q: What does a bondholder have in the issuing company?
opts: A share of ownership and profits
why: A bondholder lends money and is promised interest and the principal back.
Ownership and profit-sharing belong to shareholders, not bondholders.
A board seat comes with ownership or special rights, not a bond.
Votes on decisions come with shares, not with a bond.

q: When does a bond repay its face value?
opts: Only if the holder asks twice
why: Interest may be paid in parts, but the face value is repaid once.
Repayment does not depend on the price of the bond in the market.
The issuer repays on the date, and the holder need not ask.
Maturity is the date on which the principal is repaid.

q: How is a bond different from a share?
opts: A bond gives votes, and a share does not
A bond is a loan, a share is ownership
A bond has no risk, and a share has some
They are the same thing, in different names
why: Votes come with shares, and not with bonds at all.
A bond is a promise to pay. A share is ownership.
A bond still carries risks, such as a borrower failing.
They are different, since one is lending, one owning.

pts: A bond is a loan that pays a coupon and returns face value at maturity.
A bondholder is a lender, not an owner.
The promise is only as good as the borrower.
